Physical Activity and Function A common com-
plaint is that the basic activities of daily living, including eating, 
require eﬀ ort. Individuals with COPD often complain that they 
tire easily when eating or experience dyspnea during eating and 
drinking. Fatigue resulting from dyspnea may also interfere 
with eating. Chewing and swallowing may be impaired since 
both activities change breathing patterns and reduce oxygen
uptake. Chronic mouth breathing or certain medications may 
also cause changes in taste perceptions and/or xerostomia (dry 
mouth).
Patients with COPD often suﬀ er from hyperinﬂ ation of the 
lungs with accompanying ﬂ attening of the diaphragm and 
reduced abdominal volume, leading to unnecessary fullness
and bloating at mealtime.114 If the individual eats too much at a 
meal, the increased positive pressure applied to the diaphragm 
by the stomach results in breathing diﬃ  culty. Aerophagia
often occurs in COPD and may also cause gastric bloating. Ad-
ditional factors that may contribute to poor nutrition include 
depression and diﬃ  culty in shopping and preparing foods.
